Container.Name: GravityLAN
Container.Overview: GravityLAN is a self-hosted network radar and homelab inventory dashboard: sweeps subnets, tracks devices and IP history, draws network topology and racks, and monitors Linux hosts via an optional lightweight agent.[br][br] [b]What you get[/b][br] - Network scans with hostnames, ports, services and vendors; scan subnets and VLANs can be imported from the router (SNMP or UniFi).[br] - Health and availability: uptime, latency, flapping, SSL expiry and pending security patches per device.[br] - Topology map, racks and an IP map of every subnet.[br] - Optional Linux agent: CPU, RAM, disks, temperature, package updates over SSH, and a browser SSH terminal with an encrypted key store.[br] - Read-only API tokens, Swagger UI at /docs and a Python client; a read-only token suits AI assistants and agents (it never gets SSH, agent configuration or admin endpoints).[br] - Two web interfaces: the classic React view and GravityUI, a preview of the new interface (in development), switchable in the sidebar or under Settings → Default interface.[br][br] [b]Unraid defaults[/b][br] PUID 99 and PGID 100 (nobody:users): on start the container makes the appdata directory writable for that user. No privileged mode needed.[br][br] [b]Which network type?[/b][br] - [b]Host[/b] (default, recommended): GravityLAN uses the server's own interfaces and sees every subnet Unraid is in at Layer 2 (ARP, real MAC addresses, vendors, mDNS). Web UI at http://SERVER-IP:8000; the port is set with "Internal Port", port mappings are ignored.[br] - [b]Custom: br0[/b] (macvlan or ipvlan): the container gets its own IP in your LAN (set a fixed IP) and scans that subnet at Layer 2. Unraid and the container cannot reach each other unless "Host access to custom networks" is on under Settings → Docker.[br] - [b]VLANs[/b]: add one custom network per VLAN under "Additional Networks" (br0.10, br0.20 …) so the container gets an address in each VLAN and scans all of them at Layer 2. Create the VLAN interfaces first under Settings → Network Settings.[br] - [b]Bridge[/b]: not recommended. Hosts are only found through NAT, without MAC addresses or vendors.[br][br] [b]How scanning works[/b][br] Scheduled Nmap and ARP scans run over your scan subnets. The IP addresses page shows how each subnet is reached:[br] - [b]L2 Direct[/b]: GravityLAN has an interface in the subnet. ARP and Nmap give hosts, MAC addresses, vendors, ports and services.[br] - [b]L3 Routed[/b]: the subnet is only reachable through the router. Nmap finds hosts and services, but ARP stops at the router, so there are no MAC addresses.[br] - [b]L2 Probe[/b]: an agent inside a routed subnet with "L2 Subnet Scanner (Probe)" switched on reports the real MAC addresses.[br] The setup wizard detects your subnets; routed ones such as an IoT VLAN can be added there or later on the IP addresses page. Scanning needs NET_RAW and NET_ADMIN (already in Extra Parameters), not privileged mode.[br][br] [b]Deutsch[/b][br] GravityLAN ist ein selbst gehostetes Netzwerk-Radar und Homelab-Inventar: scannt Subnetze, verfolgt Geräte und IP-Verlauf, zeichnet Topologie und Racks und überwacht Linux-Hosts über einen optionalen schlanken Agenten.[br][br] [b]Was du bekommst[/b][br] - Netzwerk-Scans mit Hostnamen, Ports, Diensten und Herstellern; Scan-Subnetze und VLANs lassen sich vom Router importieren (SNMP oder UniFi).[br] - Health und Verfügbarkeit: Uptime, Latenz, Flackern, SSL-Ablauf und offene Sicherheits-Patches pro Gerät.[br] - Topologie-Karte, Racks und eine IP-Karte jedes Subnetzes.[br] - Optionaler Linux-Agent: CPU, RAM, Laufwerke, Temperatur, Paket-Updates per SSH, dazu ein SSH-Terminal im Browser mit verschlüsseltem Key-Store.[br] - Schreibgeschützte API-Token, Swagger UI unter /docs und ein Python-Client; ein schreibgeschütztes Token eignet sich für KI-Assistenten und Agenten (es bekommt nie SSH, Agent-Konfiguration oder Admin-Endpunkte).[br] - Zwei Weboberflächen: die klassische React-Ansicht und GravityUI, eine Vorschau der neuen Oberfläche (in Entwicklung), umschaltbar in der Seitenleiste oder unter Einstellungen → Standard-Oberfläche.[br][br] [b]Unraid-Vorgaben[/b][br] PUID 99 und PGID 100 (nobody:users): Beim Start macht der Container den Appdata-Ordner für diesen Benutzer beschreibbar. Kein Privileged-Modus nötig.[br][br] [b]Welcher Netzwerktyp?[/b][br] - [b]Host[/b] (Standard, empfohlen): GravityLAN nutzt die Schnittstellen des Servers und sieht jedes Subnetz, in dem Unraid hängt, auf Layer 2 (ARP, echte MAC-Adressen, Hersteller, mDNS). Weboberfläche unter http://SERVER-IP:8000; der Port wird über "Internal Port" gesetzt, Port-Mappings werden ignoriert.[br] - [b]Custom: br0[/b] (macvlan oder ipvlan): Der Container bekommt eine eigene IP im LAN (feste IP eintragen) und scannt dieses Subnetz auf Layer 2. Unraid und Container erreichen sich gegenseitig nur, wenn unter Settings → Docker "Host access to custom networks" eingeschaltet ist.[br] - [b]VLANs[/b]: Unter "Additional Networks" je VLAN ein Custom-Netz hinzufügen (br0.10, br0.20 …). Dann hat der Container in jedem VLAN eine Adresse und scannt alle auf Layer 2. Die VLAN-Schnittstellen vorher unter Settings → Network Settings anlegen.[br] - [b]Bridge[/b]: nicht empfohlen. Hosts werden nur durch NAT gefunden, ohne MAC-Adressen und Hersteller.[br][br] [b]So wird gescannt[/b][br] Geplante Nmap- und ARP-Scans laufen über deine Scan-Subnetze. Die Seite IP-Adressen zeigt, wie jedes Subnetz erreicht wird:[br] - [b]L2 Direkt[/b]: GravityLAN hat eine Schnittstelle im Subnetz. ARP und Nmap liefern Hosts, MAC-Adressen, Hersteller, Ports und Dienste.[br] - [b]L3 Geroutet[/b]: Das Subnetz ist nur über den Router erreichbar. Nmap findet Hosts und Dienste, aber ARP endet am Router, daher gibt es keine MAC-Adressen.[br] - [b]L2 Probe[/b]: Ein Agent im gerouteten Subnetz mit eingeschaltetem "L2 Subnetz-Scanner (Probe)" meldet die echten MAC-Adressen.[br] Der Setup-Wizard erkennt deine Subnetze; geroutete wie ein IoT-VLAN lassen sich dort oder später auf der Seite IP-Adressen ergänzen. Zum Scannen braucht der Container NET_RAW und NET_ADMIN (stehen schon in Extra Parameters), keinen Privileged-Modus.
Container.Requires: Host network (default) or a custom br0 network with its own IP; add br0.X under "Additional Networks" for VLANs. Bridge hides MAC addresses. / Host-Netzwerk (Standard) oder ein Custom-br0-Netz mit eigener IP; für VLANs br0.X unter "Additional Networks" ergänzen. Bridge verbirgt MAC-Adressen.
Container.Description:
GravityLAN is a self-hosted dashboard and network radar for your homelab or home network.
Features: - Discovery: Scheduled Nmap and ARP network scans (hostnames, open ports, services, vendors, VLANs). - Network Inventory: Real-time SLA radar, latency telemetry, IP change logs, and offline flap detection. - Topology & Racks: Visual interactive network map with link speeds and rack unit placement. - In-Browser SSH Terminal: Fast multi-tab web terminal with saved credentials and encrypted vault. - Linux Agent (optional): Single-script monitoring for CPU, RAM, disks, temperatures, and pending package updates. - API: Read-only tokens, Swagger UI and a Python client, suited to AI assistants and agents. - GravityUI: preview of the new interface, next to the classic view.
Note: GravityLAN uses host networking mode by default to ensure direct Layer-2 ARP detection and Nmap raw socket access across your local subnets.
Container.Changes:
### 0.7.0 - GravityUI is the default interface; the classic React view stays one more release as a fallback (Settings, System, Default interface) and is removed after that. Backups now contain rack equipment, ports and cables. Images are built and published by CI, release candidates first appear as the next tag. The unused scan profiles endpoint is gone.
### 0.6.0 - Racks rebuilt: faceplates that look like the hardware, drag and drop with snapping and undo, rack equipment (patch panels, UPS, power strips, blanks, cable management), ports and cables with a front and a rear view. Backup links and a resilience view on the orbit map, single points of failure on Health. Company demo network. Design critique fixes with a readable type floor, smooth dashboard scrolling, dnspython 2.9.0.
### 0.5.6 - Follow-ups to the 0.5.5 security fixes: install command uses the server URL and needs an explicit opt-in over HTTP, bounded live discovery, install codes and open streams revoked on import and reset. Backups include device interfaces. GravityUI overview leads with network status, names problem devices and has 44 px touch targets on phones. Agent 0.3.10.
### 0.5.5 - Security fixes from an external review (thanks @schaefer-informationstechnik): settings tokens can no longer reopen setup, safe service links, bounded scans, SSH host keys checked on agent deploy, no SSH fallback to the Docker host, clean backup imports, database reset revokes old access. The manual agent install needs HTTPS or ALLOW_INSECURE=1; new options Allow Insecure Agent Install and Docker Host IP.
### 0.5.4 - Tutorials page (DE/EN) for setup, VLANs, agents, SSH and Unraid; About page; default UI switch (React or GravityUI); security patch badges on the dashboard; phone and orbit map fixes.
### 0.5.3 - Docker: PUID and PGID (template: 99/100); the container makes the data directory writable for them on start, so a fresh appdata directory no longer stops it with a permission error.
### 0.5.2 - Deleting a device in GravityUI works again; scans pick up hostnames from mDNS, NetBIOS and the system resolver.
### 0.5.1 - Package updates accept a sudo password for key logins; GravityUI no longer reports sleeping clients as disrupted.
### 0.5.0 - GravityUI, a preview of the new interface, with every page of the classic view, an orbit map and racks.
Full changelog: https://github.com/SleeperXr/GravityLAN/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: The HTTP port on which the GravityLAN WebUI and REST API are served.

Config.Name: Data Storage
Config.Description: Directory to store persistent data (SQLite database, SSH key vault, backups).

Config.Name: Internal Port
Config.Description: Container internal listening port (matches WebUI port).

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User ID the server runs as. On start the container makes the Data Storage directory writable for it. Unraid default: 99 (nobody).

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group ID the server runs as. Unraid default: 100 (users).

Config.Name: Allow Insecure Agent Install
Config.Description: Let the manual agent install command (curl | sudo bash) download over plain HTTP without ALLOW_INSECURE=1. The agent runs as root and its token travels unencrypted, so only enable this on a trusted network. Better: an HTTPS server URL behind a reverse proxy, or SSH deploy.

Config.Name: Docker Host IP
Config.Description: LAN IP of this Unraid server. Only SSH logins (agent deploy, updates, terminal) to this address may retry over the Docker bridge gateway, needed when the container can't reach its own host, e.g. with macvlan. Leave empty if not needed.

Config.Name: Debug Mode
Config.Description: Enable detailed logging for debugging scanner and backend issues.
